title: ब्राह्मपर्व · अध्याय २

items.text:
शृणुष्वेदं महाबाहो पुराणं पञ्चलक्षणम् ।
यच्छ्रुत्वा मुच्यते राजन्पुरुषो ब्रह्महत्यया ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
śṛṇuṣvedaṃ mahābāho purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam |
yacchrutvā mucyate rājanpuruṣo brahmahatyayā || 1 ||
items.speaker: सुमन्तुरुवाच
items.en: Listen to this Purana of five marks, O mighty-armed one. Hearing it, a person, O king, is freed from the sin of killing a Brahmin.

items.text:
पर्वाणि चात्र वै पञ्च कीर्तितानि स्वयम्भुवा ।
प्रथमं कथ्यते ब्राह्मं द्वितीयं वैष्णवं स्मृतम् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
parvāṇi cātra vai pañca kīrtitāni svayambhuvā |
prathamaṃ kathyate brāhmaṃ dvitīyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ smṛtam || 2 ||
items.en: Five sections of it were declared by the self-born Brahma. The first is called Brahma, the second is remembered as Vaishnava.

items.text:
तृतीयं शैवमाख्यातं चतुर्थं त्वाष्ट्रमुच्यते ।
पञ्चमं प्रतिसर्गाख्यं सर्वलोकैः सुपूजितम् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
tṛtīyaṃ śaivamākhyātaṃ caturthaṃ tvāṣṭramucyate |
pañcamaṃ pratisargākhyaṃ sarvalokaiḥ supūjitam || 3 ||
items.en: The third is called Shaiva, the fourth is called Tvashtra, and the fifth is named Pratisarga, honoured by all the worlds.

items.text:
एतानि तात पर्वाणि लक्षणानि निबोध मे ।
सर्गश्च प्रतिसर्गश्च वंशो मन्वन्तराणि च ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
etāni tāta parvāṇi lakṣaṇāni nibodha me |
sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca || 4 ||
items.en: Learn from me, my dear, the marks of these sections: creation, secondary creation, lineages, the ages of the Manus,

items.text:
वंशानुचरितं चैव पुराणं पञ्चलक्षणम् ।
चतुर्दशभिर्विद्याभिर्भूषितं कुरुनन्दन ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam |
caturdaśabhirvidyābhirbhūṣitaṃ kurunandana || 5 ||
items.en: and the deeds of the lineages. This is the Purana of five marks, adorned with the fourteen branches of learning, O joy of the Kurus.

items.text:
अङ्गानि चतुरो वेदा मीमांसा न्यायविस्तरः ।
पुराणं धर्मशास्त्रं च विद्या ह्येताश्चतुर्दश ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
aṅgāni caturo vedā mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ |
purāṇaṃ dharmaśāstraṃ ca vidyā hyetāścaturdaśa || 6 ||
items.en: The six Vedangas, the four Vedas, Mimamsa, the wide science of logic, the Purana and the law books: these are the fourteen branches of learning.

items.text:
आयुर्वेदो धनुर्वेदो गान्धर्वश्चैव ते त्रयः ।
अर्थशास्त्रं चतुर्थं तु विद्या ह्यष्टादशैव ताः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
āyurvedo dhanurvedo gāndharvaścaiva te trayaḥ |
arthaśāstraṃ caturthaṃ tu vidyā hyaṣṭādaśaiva tāḥ || 7 ||
items.en: Medicine, archery and music are those three; the science of wealth is the fourth. These make the eighteen branches of learning.

items.text:
प्रथमं कथ्यते सर्गो भूतानामिह सर्वशः ।
यच्छ्रुत्वा पापनिर्मुक्तो याति शान्तिमनुत्तमाम् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
prathamaṃ kathyate sargo bhūtānāmiha sarvaśaḥ |
yacchrutvā pāpanirmukto yāti śāntimanuttamām || 8 ||
items.en: First, the creation of beings is told here in full. Hearing it, one is freed from sin and attains the highest peace.

items.text:
जगदासीत्पुरा तात तमोभूतमलक्षणम् ।
अविज्ञेयमतर्क्यं च प्रसुप्तमिव सर्वशः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
jagadāsītpurā tāta tamobhūtamalakṣaṇam |
avijñeyamatarkyaṃ ca prasuptamiva sarvaśaḥ || 9 ||
items.en: In the beginning, my dear, the world was dark, without any mark, unknowable, beyond reasoning, as if fast asleep on every side.

items.text:
ततः स भगवानीशो ह्यव्यक्तो व्यञ्जयन्निदम् ।
महाभूतानि वृत्तौजाः प्रोत्थितस्तमनाशनः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa bhagavānīśo hyavyakto vyañjayannidam |
mahābhūtāni vṛttaujāḥ protthitastamanāśanaḥ || 10 ||
items.en: Then that lord, unmanifest, showing forth this world and the great elements, rose up, mighty and dispelling the darkness.

items.text:
योऽसावतीन्द्रियोऽग्राह्यः सूक्ष्मोऽव्यक्तः सनातनः ।
सर्वभूतमयोऽचिन्त्यः स एष स्वयमुत्थितः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
yo'sāvatīndriyo'grāhyaḥ sūkṣmo'vyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ |
sarvabhūtamayo'cintyaḥ sa eṣa svayamutthitaḥ || 11 ||
items.en: He who is beyond the senses, cannot be grasped, is subtle, unmanifest and eternal, made of all beings and beyond thought, rose up by himself.

items.text:
योऽसौ षड्विंशको लोके तथा यः पुरुषोत्तमः ।
भास्करश्च महाबाहो परं ब्रह्म च कथ्यते ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
yo'sau ṣaḍviṃśako loke tathā yaḥ puruṣottamaḥ |
bhāskaraśca mahābāho paraṃ brahma ca kathyate || 12 ||
items.en: He who is the twenty-sixth principle in the world, who is the best of persons, the sun, O mighty-armed one, is also called the supreme Brahman.

items.text:
सोऽभिध्याय शरीरात्स्वात्सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः ।
अत एव ससर्जादौ तासु वीर्यमवासृजत् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
so'bhidhyāya śarīrātsvātsisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ |
ata eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryamavāsṛjat || 13 ||
items.en: Wishing to create many kinds of creatures, he thought on them and first created from his own body; in them he placed his seed.

items.text:
यस्मादुत्पद्यते सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम् ।
बीजं शुक्रं तथा रेत उग्रं वीर्यं च कथ्यते ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
yasmādutpadyate sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam |
bījaṃ śukraṃ tathā reta ugraṃ vīryaṃ ca kathyate || 14 ||
items.en: That from which everything is born, with gods, demons and men, is called seed, semen and fierce potency.

items.text:
वीर्यस्यैतानि नामानि कथितानि स्वयम्भुवा ।
तदण्डमभवद्धैमं ज्वालामालाकुलं विभो ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
vīryasyaitāni nāmāni kathitāni svayambhuvā |
tadaṇḍamabhavaddhaimaṃ jvālāmālākulaṃ vibho || 15 ||
items.en: These are the names of that seed, told by the self-born one. It became a golden egg, O lord, surrounded by a garland of flames.

items.text:
यस्मिञ्जज्ञे स्वयं ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकपितामहः ।
सुरज्येष्ठश्चतुर्वक्त्रः परमेष्ठी पितामहः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
yasmiñjajñe svayaṃ brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ |
surajyeṣṭhaścaturvaktraḥ parameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ || 16 ||
items.en: In it Brahma himself was born, grandfather of all the worlds, eldest of the gods, four-faced, the supreme one, the grandfather.

items.text:
क्षेत्रज्ञः पुरुषो वेधाः शम्भुर्नारायणस्तथा ।
पर्यायवाचकैः शब्दैरेव ब्रह्मा प्रकीर्त्यते ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
kṣetrajñaḥ puruṣo vedhāḥ śambhurnārāyaṇastathā |
paryāyavācakaiḥ śabdaireva brahmā prakīrtyate || 17 ||
items.en: Knower of the field, the Person, the creator, Shambhu and Narayana: by such synonymous words Brahma is praised.

items.text:
सदा मनीषिभिस्तात विरञ्चिः कञ्जजस्तथा।
आपो नारा इति प्रोक्ता आपो वै नरसूनवः ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
sadā manīṣibhistāta virañciḥ kañjajastathā|
āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ || 18 ||
items.en: The wise always call him Virinchi and the lotus-born. The waters are called "nara", for the waters are the children of the Person.

items.text:
ता यदस्यायनं पूर्वं तेन नारायणः स्मृतः ।
अरमित्येव शीघ्राय नियताः कविभिः कृताः ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
tā yadasyāyanaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ |
aramityeva śīghrāya niyatāḥ kavibhiḥ kṛtāḥ || 19 ||
items.en: Because they were his first resting place, he is remembered as Narayana. The poets fixed the word "ara" for speed.

items.text:
आप एवार्णवीभूत्वा सुशीघ्रास्तेन ता नराः ।
यत्तत्कारणमव्यक्तं नित्यं सदसदात्मकम् ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
āpa evārṇavībhūtvā suśīghrāstena tā narāḥ |
yattatkāraṇamavyaktaṃ nityaṃ sadasadātmakam || 20 ||
items.en: The waters themselves became an ocean, and so they are very swift. The unmanifest cause, eternal, both being and non-being,

items.text:
तद्विसृष्टः स पुरुषो लोके ब्रह्मेति कीर्त्त्यते ।
एवं स भगवानण्डे तत्त्वमेव निरूप्य वै ॥ २ ॥
ध्यानमास्थाय राजेन्द्र तदण्डमकरोद्द्विधा ।
शकलाभ्यां च राजेन्द्र दिवं भूमिं च निर्ममे ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
tadvisṛṣṭaḥ sa puruṣo loke brahmeti kīrttyate |
evaṃ sa bhagavānaṇḍe tattvameva nirūpya vai || 2 ||
dhyānamāsthāya rājendra tadaṇḍamakaroddvidhā |
śakalābhyāṃ ca rājendra divaṃ bhūmiṃ ca nirmame || 22 ||
items.en: released by that, the Person is called Brahma in the world. Thus the lord, having understood the truth within the egg, entered meditation, O best of kings, and split that egg in two. From the two halves he made heaven and earth.

items.text:
अन्तर्व्योम दिशश्चाष्टौ वारुणं स्थानमेव हि ।
ऊर्ध्वं महान्गतो राजन् समन्ताल्लोकभूतये ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
antarvyoma diśaścāṣṭau vāruṇaṃ sthānameva hi |
ūrdhvaṃ mahāngato rājan samantāllokabhūtaye || 23 ||
items.en: Between them he made the sky, the eight directions and the place of the waters. The great one went upward, O king, to bring the worlds into being on every side.

items.text:
महतश्चाप्यहंकारस्तस्माच्च त्रिगुणा अपि ।
त्रिगुणा अतिसूक्ष्मास्तु बुद्धिगम्या हि भारत ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
mahataścāpyahaṃkārastasmācca triguṇā api |
triguṇā atisūkṣmāstu buddhigamyā hi bhārata || 24 ||
items.en: From the great principle came the sense of self, and from that the three qualities as well. The three qualities are very subtle, understood only by the mind, O descendant of Bharata.

items.text:
उत्पत्तिहेतुभूता वै भूतानां महतां नृप ।
तेषामेव गृहीतानि शनैः पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि तु ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
utpattihetubhūtā vai bhūtānāṃ mahatāṃ nṛpa |
teṣāmeva gṛhītāni śanaiḥ pañcendriyāṇi tu || 25 ||
items.en: They are the cause of the birth of the great elements, O king. From them the five senses were slowly taken.

items.text: तथैवावयवाः सूक्ष्माः षण्णामप्यमितौजसाम् ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr: tathaivāvayavāḥ sūkṣmāḥ ṣaṇṇāmapyamitaujasām || 26 ||
items.en: In the same way, the subtle parts of the six mighty ones of boundless power [were formed].

items.text:
संनिवेश्यात्ममात्रासु स राजन्भगवान्विभुः ।
भूतानि निर्ममे तात सर्वाणि विधिपूर्वकम् ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
saṃniveśyātmamātrāsu sa rājanbhagavānvibhuḥ |
bhūtāni nirmame tāta sarvāṇi vidhipūrvakam || 27 ||
items.en: Having placed them in the measures of himself, the lord, the all-pervading one, made all beings in due order, my dear.

items.text:
यन्मूर्त्यवयवाः सूक्ष्मास्तस्येमान्याश्रयाणि षट् ।
तस्माच्छरीरमित्याहुस्तस्य मूर्तिं मनीषिणः ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
yanmūrtyavayavāḥ sūkṣmāstasyemānyāśrayāṇi ṣaṭ |
tasmāccharīramityāhustasya mūrtiṃ manīṣiṇaḥ || 28 ||
items.en: The subtle parts of whose form are these six supports; therefore the wise call it his body and his form.

items.text:
महान्ति तानि भूतानि आविशन्ति ततो विभुम् ।
कर्मणा सह राजेन्द्र सगुणाश्चापि वै गुणाः ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
mahānti tāni bhūtāni āviśanti tato vibhum |
karmaṇā saha rājendra saguṇāścāpi vai guṇāḥ || 29 ||
items.en: Those great elements then enter the all-pervading lord, together with action, and the qualities too with their own qualities.

items.text:
तेषामिदं तु सप्तानां पुरुषाणां महौजसाम् ।
सूक्ष्माभ्यो मूर्तिमात्राभ्यः सम्भवत्यव्ययाद्वयम् ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
teṣāmidaṃ tu saptānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ mahaujasām |
sūkṣmābhyo mūrtimātrābhyaḥ sambhavatyavyayādvayam || 30 ||
items.en: From these seven mighty persons, from the subtle forms alone, the imperishable one gives rise to this pair.

items.text:
भूतादिमहतस्तात येन व्याप्तमिदं जगत् ।
तस्मादपि महाबाहो पुरुषाः पञ्च एव हि ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
bhūtādimahatastāta yena vyāptamidaṃ jagat |
tasmādapi mahābāho puruṣāḥ pañca eva hi || 31 ||
items.en: From the great principle and the origin of the elements, by which this world is pervaded, there are only five persons, O mighty-armed one.

items.text:
केचिदेवं परां तात सृष्टिमिच्छन्ति पण्डिताः ।
अन्येऽप्येवं महाबाहो प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
kecidevaṃ parāṃ tāta sṛṣṭimicchanti paṇḍitāḥ |
anye'pyevaṃ mahābāho pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ || 32 ||
items.en: Some wise men, my dear, wish for the higher creation in this way, and other thinkers, O mighty-armed one, declare it likewise.

items.text:
योऽसावात्मा परस्तात कल्पादौ सृजते तनुम् ।
प्रजनश्च महाबाहो सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
yo'sāvātmā parastāta kalpādau sṛjate tanum |
prajanaśca mahābāho sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ || 33 ||
items.en: That supreme self, my dear, at the start of an age creates a body and, wishing to create many kinds of creatures, makes birth.

items.text:
तेन सृष्टः पुद्गलस्तु प्रधानं विशते नृप ।
प्रधानं क्षोभितं तेन विकारान्युजते बहून् ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
tena sṛṣṭaḥ pudgalastu pradhānaṃ viśate nṛpa |
pradhānaṃ kṣobhitaṃ tena vikārānyujate bahūn || 34 ||
items.en: The being created by him enters the Primal Nature, O king. Stirred by him, the Primal Nature produces many changes.

items.text:
उत्पद्यते महांस्तस्मात्ततो भूतादिरेव हि ।
उत्पद्यते विशालं च भूतादेः कुरुनन्दन ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
utpadyate mahāṃstasmāttato bhūtādireva hi |
utpadyate viśālaṃ ca bhūtādeḥ kurunandana || 35 ||
items.en: From it arises the great principle, and then the origin of the elements. From the origin of the elements arises the vast, O joy of the Kurus.

items.text:
विशालाच्च हरिस्तात हरेश्चापि वृकास्तथा ।
वृकैर्मुष्णन्ति च बुधास्तस्मात्सर्वं भवेन्नृप ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
viśālācca haristāta hareścāpi vṛkāstathā |
vṛkairmuṣṇanti ca budhāstasmātsarvaṃ bhavennṛpa || 36 ||
items.en: From the vast comes Hari, my dear, and from Hari wolves also; the wise are robbed by the wolves; from this everything arises, O king. (text unclear)

items.text:
तथैषामेव राजेन्द्र प्रादुर्भवति वेगतः ।
मात्राणां कुरुशार्दूल विबोधस्तदनन्तरम् ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
tathaiṣāmeva rājendra prādurbhavati vegataḥ |
mātrāṇāṃ kuruśārdūla vibodhastadanantaram || 37 ||
items.en: In the same way, O best of kings, the awakening of these elemental measures swiftly follows in turn, O tiger of the Kurus.

items.text:
तस्मादपि हृषीकाणि विविधानि नृपोत्तम ।
तथेयं सृष्टिराख्याताऽऽराध्यतः कुरुनन्दन ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
tasmādapi hṛṣīkāṇi vividhāni nṛpottama |
tatheyaṃ sṛṣṭirākhyātā''rādhyataḥ kurunandana || 38 ||
items.en: From that also come the various senses, O best of kings. So this creation has been told, by worship, O joy of the Kurus.

items.text:
भूयो निबोध राजेन्द्र भूतानामिह विस्तरम् ।
गुणाधिकानि सर्वाणि भूतानि पृथिवीपते ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
bhūyo nibodha rājendra bhūtānāmiha vistaram |
guṇādhikāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni pṛthivīpate || 39 ||
items.en: Hear again, O best of kings, the detail of the elements here. All beings are rich in qualities, O lord of the earth.

items.text:
आकाशमादितः कृत्वा उत्तरोत्तरमेव हि ।
एकं द्वौ च तथा त्रीणि चत्वारश्चापि पञ्च च ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
ākāśamāditaḥ kṛtvā uttarottarameva hi |
ekaṃ dvau ca tathā trīṇi catvāraścāpi pañca ca || 40 ||
items.en: Starting with space, each next one in order has one, two, three, four and five qualities.

items.text:
ततः स भगवान्ब्रह्मा पद्मासनगतः प्रभुः ।
सर्वेषां तु स नामानि कर्माणि च पृथक्पृथक् ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa bhagavānbrahmā padmāsanagataḥ prabhuḥ |
sarveṣāṃ tu sa nāmāni karmāṇi ca pṛthakpṛthak || 41 ||
items.en: Then the lord Brahma, seated on the lotus, the master,

items.text:
वेदशब्देभ्य एवादौ पृथक्संस्थाश्च निर्ममे ।
कर्मोद्भवानां देवानां सोऽसृजद्देहिनां प्रभुः ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
vedaśabdebhya evādau pṛthaksaṃsthāśca nirmame |
karmodbhavānāṃ devānāṃ so'sṛjaddehināṃ prabhuḥ || 42 ||
items.en: from the words of the Veda made at the beginning the names, deeds and separate stations of all. The lord created the gods born of action, who have bodies.

items.text:
तुषितानां गणं राजन्यज्ञं चैव सनातनम् ।
दत्त्वा वीर समानेभ्यो गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr:
tuṣitānāṃ gaṇaṃ rājanyajñaṃ caiva sanātanam |
dattvā vīra samānebhyo guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam || 43 ||
items.en: He created the group of the Tushita gods, and the eternal sacrifice, O king. O hero, having given the secret eternal Brahman to his equals,

items.text:
दुदोह यज्ञसिद्धयर्थमृग्यजुः सामलक्षणम् ।
कालं कालविभक्तीश्च ग्रहानृतूंस्तथा नृप ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
dudoha yajñasiddhayarthamṛgyajuḥ sāmalakṣaṇam |
kālaṃ kālavibhaktīśca grahānṛtūṃstathā nṛpa || 44 ||
items.en: he milked out, for the success of sacrifice, the Rig, Yajus and Sama Vedas, and also time and its divisions, the planets and the seasons, O king,

items.text:
सरितः सागराञ्छैलान्समानि विषमाणि च ।
कामं क्रोधं तथा वाचं रतिं चापि कुरुद्वह ॥ ४५ ॥
items.tr:
saritaḥ sāgarāñchailānsamāni viṣamāṇi ca |
kāmaṃ krodhaṃ tathā vācaṃ ratiṃ cāpi kurudvaha || 45 ||
items.en: rivers, seas and mountains, level and rough ground, desire, anger, speech and pleasure, O best of the Kurus.

items.text:
सृष्टिं ससर्ज राजेन्द्र सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः ।
धर्माधर्मौ विवेकाय कर्मणां च तथासृजत् ॥ ४ ॥
सुखदुःखादिभिर्द्वन्द्वैः प्रजाश्चेमा न्ययोजयत् ।
अण्व्यो मात्राविनाशिन्यो दशार्धानां तु याः स्मृताः ॥ ४७ ॥
items.tr:
sṛṣṭiṃ sasarja rājendra sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ |
dharmādharmau vivekāya karmaṇāṃ ca tathāsṛjat || 4 ||
sukhaduḥkhādibhirdvandvaiḥ prajāścemā nyayojayat |
aṇvyo mātrāvināśinyo daśārdhānāṃ tu yāḥ smṛtāḥ || 47 ||
items.en: He made creation, O best of kings, wishing to create many kinds of creatures. For discernment of actions he made right and wrong. He joined these creatures with pairs such as pleasure and pain. Tiny, perishable measures, said to be the halves of tens, [made the world].

items.text:
ताभिः सर्वमिदं वीर सम्भवत्यनुपूर्वशः ।
यत्कृतं तु पुरा कर्म सन्नियुक्तेन वै नृप ॥ ४८ ॥
items.tr:
tābhiḥ sarvamidaṃ vīra sambhavatyanupūrvaśaḥ |
yatkṛtaṃ tu purā karma sanniyuktena vai nṛpa || 48 ||
items.en: By these, in due order, all this comes to be, O hero. Whatever action was done earlier by one set to it, O king,

items.text:
स तदेव स्वयं भेजे सृज्यमानं पुनः पुनः ।
हिंस्राहिंस्रे मृदुक्रूरे धर्माधर्मे ऋतानृते ॥ ४९ ॥
items.tr:
sa tadeva svayaṃ bheje sṛjyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ |
hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharme ṛtānṛte || 49 ||
items.en: he himself takes up that same action again and again as he is created: harmful or harmless, gentle or cruel, right or wrong, true or false.

items.text:
यद्यथास्याभवत्सर्गे तत्तस्य स्वयमाविशत् ।
यथा च लिङ्गान्यृतवः स्वयमेवानुपर्यये ॥ ५० ॥
items.tr:
yadyathāsyābhavatsarge tattasya svayamāviśat |
yathā ca liṅgānyṛtavaḥ svayamevānuparyaye || 50 ||
items.en: Whatever came to him in a creation enters him again by itself, as the seasons, with their signs, return of their own accord in turn.

items.text:
स्वानि स्वान्यभिपद्यन्ते तथा कर्माणि देहिनः ।
लोकस्येह विवृद्ध्यर्थं मुखबाहूरुपादतः ॥ ५१ ॥
items.tr:
svāni svānyabhipadyante tathā karmāṇi dehinaḥ |
lokasyeha vivṛddhyarthaṃ mukhabāhūrupādataḥ || 51 ||
items.en: So embodied beings take up their own deeds. For the growth of the world here, from the mouth, arms, thighs and feet,

items.text:
ब्रह्म क्षत्रं तथा चोभौ वैश्यशूद्रौ नृपोत्तम ।
मुखानि यानि चत्वारि तेभ्यो वेदा विनिःसृताः ॥ ५२ ॥
items.tr:
brahma kṣatraṃ tathā cobhau vaiśyaśūdrau nṛpottama |
mukhāni yāni catvāri tebhyo vedā viniḥsṛtāḥ || 52 ||
items.en: the Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra were made, O best of kings. From those four mouths [of Brahma] the Vedas came forth.

items.text:
ऋग्वेदसहिता तात वसिष्ठेन महात्मना ।
पूर्वान्मुखान्महाबाहो दक्षिणाच्चापि वै शृणु ॥ ५३ ॥
items.tr:
ṛgvedasahitā tāta vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā |
pūrvānmukhānmahābāho dakṣiṇāccāpi vai śṛṇu || 53 ||
items.en: The Rigveda collection, my dear, came with the great-souled Vasishtha, from the eastern mouth, and hear now of the southern one, O mighty-armed one.

items.text:
यजुर्वेदो महाराज याज्ञवल्क्येन वै सह ।
सामानि पश्चिमात्तात गौतमश्च महानृषिः ॥ ५४ ॥
items.tr:
yajurvedo mahārāja yājñavalkyena vai saha |
sāmāni paścimāttāta gautamaśca mahānṛṣiḥ || 54 ||
items.en: The Yajurveda came with Yajnavalkya, O great king; the Samas from the western mouth, with the great sage Gautama.

items.text:
अथर्ववेदो राजेन्द्र मुखाच्चाप्युत्तरान्नृप ।
ऋषिश्चापि तथा राजञ्छौनको लोकपूजितः ॥ ५५ ॥
items.tr:
atharvavedo rājendra mukhāccāpyuttarānnṛpa |
ṛṣiścāpi tathā rājañchaunako lokapūjitaḥ || 55 ||
items.en: The Atharvaveda came from the northern mouth, O best of kings, with the sage Shaunaka, honoured by the world.

items.text:
यत्तन्मुखं महाबाहो पञ्चमं लोकविश्रुतम् ।
अष्टादशपुराणानि सेतिहासानि भारत ॥ ५६ ॥
items.tr:
yattanmukhaṃ mahābāho pañcamaṃ lokaviśrutam |
aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni setihāsāni bhārata || 56 ||
items.en: And the fifth mouth, O mighty-armed one, famed in the world, from it came the eighteen Puranas with the histories, O descendant of Bharata,

items.text:
निर्गतानि ततस्तस्मान्मुखात्कुरुकुलोद्वह ।
तथान्याः स्मृतयश्चापि यमाद्या लोकपूजिताः ॥ ५७ ॥
items.tr:
nirgatāni tatastasmānmukhātkurukulodvaha |
tathānyāḥ smṛtayaścāpi yamādyā lokapūjitāḥ || 57 ||
items.en: O lift of the Kuru line; and other law books also, by Yama and others, honoured by the world.

items.text:
ततः स भगवान्देवो द्विधा देहमकारयत् ।
द्विधा कृत्वात्मनो देहमर्धेन पुरुषोऽभवत् ॥ ५८ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa bhagavāndevo dvidhā dehamakārayat |
dvidhā kṛtvātmano dehamardhena puruṣo'bhavat || 58 ||
items.en: Then the lord god divided his body in two. Having divided his body, with one half he became a man.

items.text:
अर्धेन नारी तस्यां च विराजमसृजत्प्रभुः ।
तपस्तप्त्वासृजद्यं तु स स्वयं पुरुषो विराट् ॥ ५९ ॥
items.tr:
ardhena nārī tasyāṃ ca virājamasṛjatprabhuḥ |
tapastaptvāsṛjadyaṃ tu sa svayaṃ puruṣo virāṭ || 59 ||
items.en: With the other half a woman, and in her the lord made Viraj. He, the Person, performed austerities and made Viraj.

items.text:
स चकार तपो राजन्सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः ।
पतीन्प्रजानामसृजन्महर्षीनादितो दश ॥ ६० ॥
items.tr:
sa cakāra tapo rājansisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ |
patīnprajānāmasṛjanmaharṣīnādito daśa || 60 ||
items.en: He performed austerities, O king, wishing to create many kinds of creatures. First he made ten great sages, lords of creatures.

items.text:
नारदं च भृगुं तात कं प्रचेतसमेव हि ।
पुलहं क्रतुं पुलस्त्यं च अत्रिमङ्गिरसं तथा ॥ ६१ ॥
items.tr:
nāradaṃ ca bhṛguṃ tāta kaṃ pracetasameva hi |
pulahaṃ kratuṃ pulastyaṃ ca atrimaṅgirasaṃ tathā || 61 ||
items.en: Narada, Bhrigu, Ka, Prachetas, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, Atri and Angiras,

items.text:
मरीचिं चापि राजेन्द्र योऽसावाद्यः प्रजापतिः ।
एतांश्चान्यांश्च राजेन्द्र असृजद् भूरितेजसः ॥ ६२ ॥
items.tr:
marīciṃ cāpi rājendra yo'sāvādyaḥ prajāpatiḥ |
etāṃścānyāṃśca rājendra asṛjad bhūritejasaḥ || 62 ||
items.en: and Marichi, O best of kings, who is the first Prajapati. He made these and others, O best of kings, of great brilliance.

items.text:
अथ देवानृषीन्दैत्यान्सोऽसृजत्कुरुनन्दन ।
यक्षरक्षः पिशाचांश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसोऽसुरान् ॥ ६३ ॥
items.tr:
atha devānṛṣīndaityānso'sṛjatkurunandana |
yakṣarakṣaḥ piśācāṃśca gandharvāpsaraso'surān || 63 ||
items.en: Then he created gods, sages and demons, O joy of the Kurus, Yakshas, Rakshasas, Pishachas, Gandharvas, Apsarases and Asuras,

items.text:
मनुष्याणां पितॄणां च सर्पाणां चैव भारत ।
नागानां च महाबाहो ससर्ज विविधान्गणान् ॥ ६४ ॥
items.tr:
manuṣyāṇāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca sarpāṇāṃ caiva bhārata |
nāgānāṃ ca mahābāho sasarja vividhāngaṇān || 64 ||
items.en: and many groups of men, ancestors, serpents and Nagas, O descendant of Bharata, O mighty-armed one.

items.text:
क्षणरुचोऽशनिगणान्रोहितेन्द्रधनूंषि च ।
धूमकेतूंस्तथा चोल्का निर्याताञ्ज्योतिषां गणान् ॥ ६५ ॥
items.tr:
kṣaṇaruco'śanigaṇānrohitendradhanūṃṣi ca |
dhūmaketūṃstathā colkā niryātāñjyotiṣāṃ gaṇān || 65 ||
items.en: Lightning, thunderbolts, red rainbows, comets and meteors, and the groups of heavenly lights;

items.text:
मनुष्यान्किन्नरान्मत्स्यान्वराहांश्च विहङ्गमान् ।
गजानश्वानथ पशून्मृगान्व्यालांश्च भारत ॥ ६६ ॥
items.tr:
manuṣyānkinnarānmatsyānvarāhāṃśca vihaṅgamān |
gajānaśvānatha paśūnmṛgānvyālāṃśca bhārata || 66 ||
items.en: men, Kinnaras, fish, boars and birds, elephants, horses, cattle, deer and beasts of prey, O descendant of Bharata,

items.text:
कृमिकीटपतङ्गांश्च यूकालिक्षकमत्कुणान् ।
सर्वं च दंशमशकं स्थावरं च पृथग्विधम् ॥ ६७ ॥
items.tr:
kṛmikīṭapataṅgāṃśca yūkālikṣakamatkuṇān |
sarvaṃ ca daṃśamaśakaṃ sthāvaraṃ ca pṛthagvidham || 67 ||
items.en: worms, insects, moths, lice, nits and bedbugs, every biting fly and mosquito, and the many kinds of plants.

items.text:
एवं स भास्करो देवः ससर्ज भुवनत्रयम् ।
येषां तु यादृशं कर्म भूतानामिह कीर्तितम् ॥ ६८ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ sa bhāskaro devaḥ sasarja bhuvanatrayam |
yeṣāṃ tu yādṛśaṃ karma bhūtānāmiha kīrtitam || 68 ||
items.en: In this way the god Bhaskara, the sun, created the three worlds. What kind of action is told here for each being,

items.text:
कथयिष्यामि तत्सर्वं क्रमयोगं च जन्मनि ।
गजा व्याला मृगास्तात पशवश्च पृथग्विधाः ॥ ६९ ॥
items.tr:
kathayiṣyāmi tatsarvaṃ kramayogaṃ ca janmani |
gajā vyālā mṛgāstāta paśavaśca pṛthagvidhāḥ || 69 ||
items.en: I will tell all that, and the order of their births. Elephants, beasts of prey, deer, my dear, and the different kinds of cattle,

items.text:
पिशाचा मानुषास्तात रक्षांसि च जरायुजाः ।
द्विजास्तु अण्डजाः सर्पा नक्रा मत्स्याः सकच्छपाः ॥ ७० ॥
items.tr:
piśācā mānuṣāstāta rakṣāṃsi ca jarāyujāḥ |
dvijāstu aṇḍajāḥ sarpā nakrā matsyāḥ sakacchapāḥ || 70 ||
items.en: Pishachas, men, and Rakshasas are born from the womb. Birds, serpents, crocodiles, fish and tortoises are egg-born.

items.text:
एवंविधानि यानीह स्थलजान्यौदकानि च ।
स्वेदजं दंशमशकं यूकालिक्षकमत्कुणाः ॥ ७१ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃvidhāni yānīha sthalajānyaudakāni ca |
svedajaṃ daṃśamaśakaṃ yūkālikṣakamatkuṇāḥ || 71 ||
items.en: Likewise all such creatures here, land-born and water-born, and those born of sweat: biting flies, mosquitoes, lice and bedbugs.

items.text:
ऊष्मणा चोपजायन्ते यच्चान्यत्किञ्चिदीदृशम् ।
उद्भिज्जाः स्थावराः सर्वे बीजकाण्डप्ररोहिणः ॥ ७२ ॥
items.tr:
ūṣmaṇā copajāyante yaccānyatkiñcidīdṛśam |
udbhijjāḥ sthāvarāḥ sarve bījakāṇḍaprarohiṇaḥ || 72 ||
items.en: They are born of heat, and anything else like these. All plants, born by sprouting, grow from seed and stalk.

items.text:
ओषध्यः फलपाकान्ता नानाविधफलोपगाः ।
अपुष्पाः फलवन्तो ये ते वनस्पतयः स्मृताः ॥ ७३ ॥
items.tr:
oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāntā nānāvidhaphalopagāḥ |
apuṣpāḥ phalavanto ye te vanaspatayaḥ smṛtāḥ || 73 ||
items.en: Herbs end when their fruit ripens, bearing fruit of many kinds. Those that bear fruit without flowers are called vanaspatis.

items.text:
पुष्पिणः फलिनश्चैव वृक्षास्तूभयतः स्मृताः ।
गुच्छगुल्मं तु विविधं तथैव तृणजातयः ॥ ७४ ॥
items.tr:
puṣpiṇaḥ phalinaścaiva vṛkṣāstūbhayataḥ smṛtāḥ |
gucchagulmaṃ tu vividhaṃ tathaiva tṛṇajātayaḥ || 74 ||
items.en: Trees are remembered as bearing both flowers and fruit. There are many kinds of clusters and shrubs, and kinds of grass,

items.text:
बीजकाण्डरुहाण्येव प्रताना वल्ल्य एव च ।
तमसा बहुरूपेण वेष्टिताः कर्महेतुना ॥ ७५ ॥
items.tr:
bījakāṇḍaruhāṇyeva pratānā vallya eva ca |
tamasā bahurūpeṇa veṣṭitāḥ karmahetunā || 75 ||
items.en: creepers and vines growing from seed and stalk, wrapped in manifold darkness because of their past actions.

items.text:
अन्तःसंज्ञा भवन्त्येते सुखदुःखसमन्विताः ।
एतावत्यस्तु गतयः प्रोद्भूताः कुरुनन्दन ॥ ७६ ॥
items.tr:
antaḥsaṃjñā bhavantyete sukhaduḥkhasamanvitāḥ |
etāvatyastu gatayaḥ prodbhūtāḥ kurunandana || 76 ||
items.en: They have inner awareness and feel pleasure and pain. So many are the courses of birth that have arisen, O joy of the Kurus.

items.text:
तस्माद्देवाद्दीप्तिमन्तो भास्कराच्य महात्मनः ।
घोरेऽस्मिंस्तात संसारे नित्यं सततयायिनि ॥ ७७ ॥
items.tr:
tasmāddevāddīptimanto bhāskarācya mahātmanaḥ |
ghore'smiṃstāta saṃsāre nityaṃ satatayāyini || 77 ||
items.en: From that god, the radiant great-souled Bhaskara, they arise in this terrible, always moving cycle of rebirth, my dear.

items.text:
एवं सर्वं स सृष्ट्वेदं राजँल्लोकगुरुं परम् ।
तिरोभूतः स भूतात्मा कालं कालेन पीडयन् ॥ ७८ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ sarvaṃ sa sṛṣṭvedaṃ rājam̐llokaguruṃ param |
tirobhūtaḥ sa bhūtātmā kālaṃ kālena pīḍayan || 78 ||
items.en: Having created all this, O king, the supreme teacher of the worlds, the self of all beings, vanished, wearing out time with time.

items.text:
यदा स देवो जागर्ति तदेदं चेष्टते जगत् ।
यदा स्वपिति शान्तात्मा तदा सर्वं निमीलति ॥ ७९ ॥
items.tr:
yadā sa devo jāgarti tadedaṃ ceṣṭate jagat |
yadā svapiti śāntātmā tadā sarvaṃ nimīlati || 79 ||
items.en: When that god wakes, this world moves; when the peaceful one sleeps, everything closes its eyes.

items.text:
तस्मिन्स्वपिति राजेन्द्र जन्तवः कर्मबन्धनाः ।
स्वकर्मभ्यो निवर्तन्ते मनश्च ग्लानिमृच्छति ॥ ८० ॥
items.tr:
tasminsvapiti rājendra jantavaḥ karmabandhanāḥ |
svakarmabhyo nivartante manaśca glānimṛcchati || 80 ||
items.en: When he sleeps, O best of kings, creatures, bound by their deeds, turn back from their own actions, and the mind sinks into weariness.

items.text:
युगपत्तु प्रलीयन्ते यदा तस्मिन्महात्मनि ।
तदायं सर्वभूतात्मा सुखं स्वपिति भारत ॥ ८१ ॥
items.tr:
yugapattu pralīyante yadā tasminmahātmani |
tadāyaṃ sarvabhūtātmā sukhaṃ svapiti bhārata || 81 ||
items.en: When all together dissolve in that great soul, then this self of all beings sleeps in comfort, O descendant of Bharata.

items.text:
तमो यदा समाश्रित्य चिरं तिष्ठति सेन्द्रियः ।
न नवं कुरुते कर्म तदोत्क्रामति मूर्तितः ॥ ८२ ॥
items.tr:
tamo yadā samāśritya ciraṃ tiṣṭhati sendriyaḥ |
na navaṃ kurute karma tadotkrāmati mūrtitaḥ || 82 ||
items.en: When he stays long in darkness with his senses, he does no new action and leaves his bodily form.

items.text:
यदाहंमात्रिको भूत्वा बीजं स्थास्नु चरिष्णु च ।
समाविशति संसृष्टस्तदा मूतिं विमुञ्चति ॥ ८३ ॥
items.tr:
yadāhaṃmātriko bhūtvā bījaṃ sthāsnu cariṣṇu ca |
samāviśati saṃsṛṣṭastadā mūtiṃ vimuñcati || 83 ||
items.en: When he becomes only the sense of "I" and enters the seed, both still and moving, fully joined, then he lets go of the form.

items.text:
एवं स जाग्रत्स्वप्नाभ्यामिदं सर्वं जगत्प्रभुः ।
संजीवयति चाजस्रं प्रमापयति चाव्ययः ॥ ८४ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ sa jāgratsvapnābhyāmidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatprabhuḥ |
saṃjīvayati cājasraṃ pramāpayati cāvyayaḥ || 84 ||
items.en: So this lord, by waking and sleeping, ceaselessly gives life to this whole world and brings death to it, himself unchanging.

items.text:
कल्पादौ सृजते तात अन्ते कल्पस्य संहरेत् ।
दिनं तस्येह यत्तात कल्पान्तमिति कथ्यते ॥ ८५ ॥
items.tr:
kalpādau sṛjate tāta ante kalpasya saṃharet |
dinaṃ tasyeha yattāta kalpāntamiti kathyate || 85 ||
items.en: At the start of an age he creates, my dear, and at its end he withdraws. His day here is called the end of an age.

items.text:
कालसंख्यां ततस्तस्य कल्पस्य शृणु भारत ।
निमेषा दश चाष्टौ च अक्ष्णः काष्ठा निगद्यते ॥ ८६ ॥
items.tr:
kālasaṃkhyāṃ tatastasya kalpasya śṛṇu bhārata |
nimeṣā daśa cāṣṭau ca akṣṇaḥ kāṣṭhā nigadyate || 86 ||
items.en: Now hear, O descendant of Bharata, the count of time of that age. Eighteen blinks of the eye are called a kashtha.

items.text:
त्रिंशत्काष्ठाः कलामाहुः क्षणस्त्रिंशत्कलाः स्मृताः ।
मुहूर्तमथ मौहूर्ता वदन्ति द्वादश क्षणम् ॥ ८७ ॥
items.tr:
triṃśatkāṣṭhāḥ kalāmāhuḥ kṣaṇastriṃśatkalāḥ smṛtāḥ |
muhūrtamatha mauhūrtā vadanti dvādaśa kṣaṇam || 87 ||
items.en: Thirty kashthas make a kala, and thirty kalas are remembered as a kshana. Those who know hours say twelve kshanas make a muhurta.

items.text:
त्रिंशन्मुहूर्तमुद्दिष्टमहोरात्रं मनीषिभिः ।
मासस्त्रिंशदहोरात्रं द्वौ द्वौ मासावृतुः स्मृतः ॥ ८८ ॥
items.tr:
triṃśanmuhūrtamuddiṣṭamahorātraṃ manīṣibhiḥ |
māsastriṃśadahorātraṃ dvau dvau māsāvṛtuḥ smṛtaḥ || 88 ||
items.en: Thirty muhurtas are declared by the wise to be a day and night; thirty days and nights make a month; two months make a season.

items.text:
ऋतुत्रयमप्ययनमयने द्वे तु वत्सरः ।
अहोरात्रे विभजते सूर्यो मानुषदैविके ॥ ८९ ॥
items.tr:
ṛtutrayamapyayanamayane dve tu vatsaraḥ |
ahorātre vibhajate sūryo mānuṣadaivike || 89 ||
items.en: Three seasons make a half-year; two half-years make a year. The sun divides days and nights into human and divine ones.

items.text:
रात्रिः स्वप्नाय भूतानां चेष्टायै कर्मणामहः ।
पित्र्ये रात्र्यहनी मासः प्रविभागस्तु पक्षयोः ॥ ९० ॥
items.tr:
rātriḥ svapnāya bhūtānāṃ ceṣṭāyai karmaṇāmahaḥ |
pitrye rātryahanī māsaḥ pravibhāgastu pakṣayoḥ || 90 ||
items.en: Night is for the sleep of beings, day for the activity of deeds. For the ancestors, night and day make a month, and the division is by the two fortnights.

items.text:
कर्म चेष्टास्वहः कृष्णः मुक्तः स्वप्नाय शर्वरी ।
दैवे रात्र्यहनी वर्षं प्रविभागस्तयोः पुनः ॥ ९१ ॥
items.tr:
karma ceṣṭāsvahaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ muktaḥ svapnāya śarvarī |
daive rātryahanī varṣaṃ pravibhāgastayoḥ punaḥ || 91 ||
items.en: The day is for deeds and activity; the dark fortnight, and the night, for sleep. For the gods, night and day make a year, and their division is again as follows.

items.text:
अहस्तत्रोदगयनं रात्रिः स्याद्दक्षिणायनम् ।
ब्राह्मस्य तु क्षपाहस्य यत्प्रमाणं महीपते ॥ ९२ ॥
items.tr:
ahastatrodagayanaṃ rātriḥ syāddakṣiṇāyanam |
brāhmasya tu kṣapāhasya yatpramāṇaṃ mahīpate || 92 ||
items.en: The day is the northern course of the sun, and the night the southern one. Now the measure of Brahma's night and day, O lord of the earth:

items.text:
एकैकशो युगानां तु क्रमशस्तन्तिबोध मे ।
चत्वार्याहुः सहस्राणि वर्षाणां तत्कृतं युगम् ॥ ९३ ॥
items.tr:
ekaikaśo yugānāṃ tu kramaśastantibodha me |
catvāryāhuḥ sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tatkṛtaṃ yugam || 93 ||
items.en: learn from me the ages one by one in order. Four thousand years are said to make the Krita age.

items.text:
तस्य तावच्छती सन्ध्या सन्ध्यांशश्च तथाविधः ।
त्रेता त्रीणि सहस्राणि वर्षाणि च विदुर्बुधाः ॥ ९४ ॥
items.tr:
tasya tāvacchatī sandhyā sandhyāṃśaśca tathāvidhaḥ |
tretā trīṇi sahasrāṇi varṣāṇi ca vidurbudhāḥ || 94 ||
items.en: Its dawn is four hundred years, and its twilight is the same. The wise know the Treta as three thousand years.

items.text:
शतानि षट् च राजेन्द्र सन्ध्यासन्ध्यांशयोः पृथक् ।
वर्षाणां द्वे सहस्रे तु द्वापरे परिकीर्तिते ॥ ९५ ॥
items.tr:
śatāni ṣaṭ ca rājendra sandhyāsandhyāṃśayoḥ pṛthak |
varṣāṇāṃ dve sahasre tu dvāpare parikīrtite || 95 ||
items.en: Six hundred years, O best of kings, are for its dawn and twilight separately. The Dvapara is declared to be two thousand years.

items.text:
चत्वारि च शतान्याहुः सन्ध्यासन्ध्यांशयोर्बुधः ।
सहस्रं कथितं तिष्ये शतद्वयसमन्वितम् ॥ ९६ ॥
items.tr:
catvāri ca śatānyāhuḥ sandhyāsandhyāṃśayorbudhaḥ |
sahasraṃ kathitaṃ tiṣye śatadvayasamanvitam || 96 ||
items.en: The wise say its dawn and twilight are four hundred. The Tishya [Kali] is told to be a thousand years with two hundred more.

items.text:
एषा चतुर्युगस्यापि संख्या प्रोक्ता नृपोत्तम ।
यदेतत्परिसंख्या तमादावेव चतुर्युगम् ॥ ९७ ॥
items.tr:
eṣā caturyugasyāpi saṃkhyā proktā nṛpottama |
yadetatparisaṃkhyā tamādāveva caturyugam || 97 ||
items.en: This is the count of the four ages, O best of kings. Taken together, it is a set of four ages.

items.text:
एतद्द्वादशसाहस्रं देवानां युगमुच्यते ।
दैविकानां युगानां तु सहस्रपरिसंख्यया ॥ ९८ ॥
items.tr:
etaddvādaśasāhasraṃ devānāṃ yugamucyate |
daivikānāṃ yugānāṃ tu sahasraparisaṃkhyayā || 98 ||
items.en: This is called a divine age of twelve thousand years. A thousand such divine ages by count

items.text:
ब्राह्ममेकमहर्ज्ञेयं तावती रात्रिरुच्यते ।
एतद्युगसहस्रान्तं ब्राह्मं पुण्यमहर्विदुः ॥ ९९ ॥
items.tr:
brāhmamekamaharjñeyaṃ tāvatī rātrirucyate |
etadyugasahasrāntaṃ brāhmaṃ puṇyamaharviduḥ || 99 ||
items.en: are to be known as one day of Brahma, and the night is said to be as long. Those who know say the holy day of Brahma ends after a thousand ages.

items.text:
रात्रिं च तावतीमेव तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ।
ततोऽसौ युगपर्यन्ते प्रसुप्तः प्रतिबुध्यते ॥ १०० ॥
items.tr:
rātriṃ ca tāvatīmeva te'horātravido janāḥ |
tato'sau yugaparyante prasuptaḥ pratibudhyate || 100 ||
items.en: The people who know day and night say the night is of the same length. Then at the end of the ages, he who was asleep wakes.

items.text:
प्रतिबुद्धस्तु सृजति मनः सदसदात्मकम् ।
मनः सृष्टिं विकुरुते चोद्यमानं सिसृक्षया ॥ १०१ ॥
items.tr:
pratibuddhastu sṛjati manaḥ sadasadātmakam |
manaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ vikurute codyamānaṃ sisṛkṣayā || 101 ||
items.en: Awake, he creates the mind, which is both being and non-being. Urged by the wish to create, the mind transforms creation.

items.text:
विपुलं जायते तस्मात्तस्य शब्दं गुणं विदुः ।
विपुलात्तु विकुर्वाणात्सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिः ॥ १०२ ॥
items.tr:
vipulaṃ jāyate tasmāttasya śabdaṃ guṇaṃ viduḥ |
vipulāttu vikurvāṇātsarvagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ || 102 ||
items.en: From it arises the vast [space], whose quality the wise say is sound. From the vast, as it changes, comes the pure, scent-bearing

items.text:
बलवाञ्जायते वायुः स वै स्पर्शगुणो मतः ।
वायोरपि विकुर्वाणाद्विरोचिष्णु तमोनुदम् ॥ १०३ ॥
items.tr:
balavāñjāyate vāyuḥ sa vai sparśaguṇo mataḥ |
vāyorapi vikurvāṇādvirociṣṇu tamonudam || 103 ||
items.en: powerful wind, which is held to have the quality of touch. From the wind, as it changes, comes the shining, darkness-removing

items.text:
उत्पद्यते विचित्रांशुस्तस्य रूपं गुणं विदुः ।
तस्मादपि विकुर्वाणादापो जाताः स्मृता बुधैः ॥ १०४ ॥
items.tr:
utpadyate vicitrāṃśustasya rūpaṃ guṇaṃ viduḥ |
tasmādapi vikurvāṇādāpo jātāḥ smṛtā budhaiḥ || 104 ||
items.en: fire, of many-coloured rays, whose quality they say is form. From it, as it changes, the waters are remembered by the wise to be born.

items.text:
तासां गुणो रसो ज्ञेयः सर्वलोकस्य भावनः।
अद्भ्यो गन्धगुणा भूमिरित्येषा सृष्टिरादितः ॥ १०५ ॥
items.tr:
tāsāṃ guṇo raso jñeyaḥ sarvalokasya bhāvanaḥ|
adbhyo gandhaguṇā bhūmirityeṣā sṛṣṭirāditaḥ || 105 ||
items.en: The quality of the waters is to be known as taste, the nourisher of all the world. From the waters, the earth has the quality of smell. Such is the creation from the beginning.

items.text:
यत्प्राग्द्वादशसाहस्रमुक्तं सौमनसं युगम् ।
तदेकसप्ततिगुणं मन्वन्तरमिहोच्यते ॥ १०६ ॥
items.tr:
yatprāgdvādaśasāhasramuktaṃ saumanasaṃ yugam |
tadekasaptatiguṇaṃ manvantaramihocyate || 106 ||
items.en: The age of twelve thousand [divine years] told before, the Saumanasa age, multiplied seventy-one times, is here called a Manvantara.

items.text:
मन्वन्तराण्यसंख्यानि सर्गः संहार एव च ।
तथाप्यहे सदा ब्राह्मे मनवस्तु चतुर्दश ॥ १०७ ॥
items.tr:
manvantarāṇyasaṃkhyāni sargaḥ saṃhāra eva ca |
tathāpyahe sadā brāhme manavastu caturdaśa || 107 ||
items.en: Manvantaras are countless, and so are creation and dissolution. Still, in the day of Brahma there are always fourteen Manus.

items.text:
कथ्यन्ते कुरुशार्दूल संख्यया पण्डितैः सदा ।
मनोः स्वायम्भुवस्येह षड्वंश्या मनवोऽपरे ॥ १०८ ॥
items.tr:
kathyante kuruśārdūla saṃkhyayā paṇḍitaiḥ sadā |
manoḥ svāyambhuvasyeha ṣaḍvaṃśyā manavo'pare || 108 ||
items.en: They are always told by the learned by number, O tiger of the Kurus. Beside the Svayambhuva Manu here, six other Manus come from his line.

items.text:
सृष्टवन्तः प्रजाः स्वाःस्वाः महात्मानो महौजसः ।
सावर्णेयस्तथा पञ्चभौत्यो रौच्यस्तथापरः ॥ १०९ ॥
items.tr:
sṛṣṭavantaḥ prajāḥ svāḥsvāḥ mahātmāno mahaujasaḥ |
sāvarṇeyastathā pañcabhautyo raucyastathāparaḥ || 109 ||
items.en: The mighty great souls created their own creatures. [The others are] Savarneya, Panchabhautya and Raucya.

items.text:
एते भविष्या मनवः सप्त प्रोक्ता नृपोत्तम ।
स्वस्वेऽन्तरे सर्वमिदं पालयन्ति चराचरम् ॥ ११० ॥
items.tr:
ete bhaviṣyā manavaḥ sapta proktā nṛpottama |
svasve'ntare sarvamidaṃ pālayanti carācaram || 110 ||
items.en: These seven Manus, O best of kings, are said to be those to come. In their own periods they protect all this, moving and unmoving.

items.text:
एवंविधं दिनं तस्य विरिञ्चेस्तु महात्मनः ।
तस्यान्ते कुरुते सर्गं यथेदं कथितं तव ॥ १११ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃvidhaṃ dinaṃ tasya viriñcestu mahātmanaḥ |
tasyānte kurute sargaṃ yathedaṃ kathitaṃ tava || 111 ||
items.en: Such is the day of the great-souled Virinchi [Brahma]. At its end he makes creation, as I have told you.

items.text:
क्रीडन्निवैतत्कुरुते परमेष्ठी नराधिप ।
चतुष्पात्सकलो धर्मः सत्यं चैव कृते युगे ॥ ११२ ॥
items.tr:
krīḍannivaitatkurute parameṣṭhī narādhipa |
catuṣpātsakalo dharmaḥ satyaṃ caiva kṛte yuge || 112 ||
items.en: The supreme one does this as if playing, O ruler of men. In the Krita age duty stands on all four feet, and so does truth.

items.text:
नाधर्मेणागमः कश्चिन्मनुष्याणां प्रवर्तते ।
इतरेष्वागमास्तात धर्मश्च कुरुनन्दन ॥ ११३ ॥
items.tr:
nādharmeṇāgamaḥ kaścinmanuṣyāṇāṃ pravartate |
itareṣvāgamāstāta dharmaśca kurunandana || 113 ||
items.en: No gain by wrong means comes to men. In the other ages, my dear, gains and duty [change], O joy of the Kurus,

items.text:
यादृशाः परिहीयन्ते यथाह भगवान्मनुः।
चौर्याच्चाप्यनृताद्राजन्मायाभिरमितद्युते ॥ ११४ ॥
items.tr:
yādṛśāḥ parihīyante yathāha bhagavānmanuḥ|
cauryāccāpyanṛtādrājanmāyābhiramitadyute || 114 ||
items.en: as they decline, as the lord Manu says: through theft, falsehood and tricks, O king of boundless splendour.

items.text:
पादेन हीयते धर्मस्त्रेतादिषु युगेषु वै ।
अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्थाश्चतुर्वर्षशतायुषः ॥ ११५ ॥
items.tr:
pādena hīyate dharmastretādiṣu yugeṣu vai |
arogāḥ sarvasiddhārthāścaturvarṣaśatāyuṣaḥ || 115 ||
items.en: In the Treta and later ages duty loses one quarter at a time. People were free of disease, all their aims were met, and they lived four hundred years.

items.text:
कृतत्रेतादिषु त्वेषां वयो ह्रसति पादशः ।
वेदोक्तमायुराशीश्च मर्त्यानां कुरुनन्दन ॥ ११६ ॥
items.tr:
kṛtatretādiṣu tveṣāṃ vayo hrasati pādaśaḥ |
vedoktamāyurāśīśca martyānāṃ kurunandana || 116 ||
items.en: In the Krita, Treta and the rest, their life span shrinks quarter by quarter, and so does the life told in the Vedas and the blessings of mortals, O joy of the Kurus.

items.text:
कर्मणां तु फलं तात फलत्यनुयुगं सदा ।
प्रभावश्च तथा लोके फलत्येव शरीरिणाम् ॥ ११७ ॥
items.tr:
karmaṇāṃ tu phalaṃ tāta phalatyanuyugaṃ sadā |
prabhāvaśca tathā loke phalatyeva śarīriṇām || 117 ||
items.en: The fruit of deeds, my dear, ripens in every age, and the power of embodied beings also bears fruit in the world.

items.text:
अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास्त्रेतायां द्वापरे परे ।
अन्ये कलियुगे नृणां युगधर्मानुरूपतः ॥ ११८ ॥
items.tr:
anye kṛtayuge dharmāstretāyāṃ dvāpare pare |
anye kaliyuge nṛṇāṃ yugadharmānurūpataḥ || 118 ||
items.en: The duties are one thing in the Krita age, another in the Treta, another after that in the Dvapara, and another for people in the Kali age, suited to the duty of each age.

items.text:
तपः परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ज्ञानमुच्यते ।
द्वापरे यज्ञमित्याहुर्दानमेकं कलौ युगे ॥ ११९ ॥
items.tr:
tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānamucyate |
dvāpare yajñamityāhurdānamekaṃ kalau yuge || 119 ||
items.en: Austerity is supreme in the Krita age, knowledge in the Treta; they say sacrifice in the Dvapara and giving alone in the Kali age.

items.text:
सर्वस्य राजन्सर्गस्य गुप्त्यर्थं च महाद्युते ।
मुखबाहूरुपादानां पृथक्कर्माण्यकल्पयत् ॥ १२० ॥
items.tr:
sarvasya rājansargasya guptyarthaṃ ca mahādyute |
mukhabāhūrupādānāṃ pṛthakkarmāṇyakalpayat || 120 ||
items.en: To protect all creation, O radiant king, he assigned separate duties to those from the mouth, arms, thighs and feet.

items.text:
अध्यापनमध्ययनं यजनं याजनं तथा ।
दानं प्रतिग्रहं चैव ब्राह्मणानामकल्पयत् ॥ १२१ ॥
items.tr:
adhyāpanamadhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ yājanaṃ tathā |
dānaṃ pratigrahaṃ caiva brāhmaṇānāmakalpayat || 121 ||
items.en: Teaching, studying, performing sacrifice, conducting sacrifice for others, giving, and receiving gifts: these he assigned to Brahmins.

items.text:
प्रजानां पालनं राजन्दानमध्ययनं तथा ।
विषयेषु प्रसक्तिं च तथेज्यां क्षत्रियस्य तु ॥ १२२ ॥
items.tr:
prajānāṃ pālanaṃ rājandānamadhyayanaṃ tathā |
viṣayeṣu prasaktiṃ ca tathejyāṃ kṣatriyasya tu || 122 ||
items.en: Protecting the people, O king, giving, studying, attachment to sense objects [in due measure] and offering sacrifice: these he assigned to the Kshatriya.

items.text:
पशूनां रक्षणं दानमिज्याध्ययनमेव च ।
वणिक्पथं कुसीदं च वैश्यस्य कृषिरेव च ॥ १२३ ॥
items.tr:
paśūnāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dānamijyādhyayanameva ca |
vaṇikpathaṃ kusīdaṃ ca vaiśyasya kṛṣireva ca || 123 ||
items.en: Guarding cattle, giving, sacrifice and study, trade, lending at interest and farming are for the Vaishya.

items.text:
एकमेव तु शूद्रस्य कर्म लोके प्रकीर्तितम् ।
एतेषामेव वर्णानां शुश्रूषामनुपूर्वशः ॥ १२४ ॥
items.tr:
ekameva tu śūdrasya karma loke prakīrtitam |
eteṣāmeva varṇānāṃ śuśrūṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ || 124 ||
items.en: Only one work is declared for the Shudra in the world: service of these same classes in due order.

items.text:
पुरुषस्य सदा श्रेष्ठं नाभेरूर्ध्वं नृपोत्तम ।
तस्मादपि शुचितरं मुखं तात स्वयम्भुवः ॥ १२५ ॥
items.tr:
puruṣasya sadā śreṣṭhaṃ nābherūrdhvaṃ nṛpottama |
tasmādapi śucitaraṃ mukhaṃ tāta svayambhuvaḥ || 125 ||
items.en: The part of a person above the navel is always the best, O best of kings. And even purer than that is the mouth of the self-born one.

items.text:
तस्मान्मुखाद्द्विजो जात इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ।
सर्वस्यैवास्य धर्मस्य धर्मतो ब्राह्मणः प्रभुः ॥ १२६ ॥
items.tr:
tasmānmukhāddvijo jāta itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ |
sarvasyaivāsya dharmasya dharmato brāhmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ || 126 ||
items.en: "The Brahmin was born from the mouth": so says the Vedic scripture. By right, the Brahmin is the lord of all this duty.

items.text:
स सृष्टो ब्रह्मणा पूर्वं तपस्तप्त्वा कुरूद्वह ।
हव्यानामिव कव्यानां सर्वस्यापि च गुप्तये ॥ १२७ ॥
items.tr:
sa sṛṣṭo brahmaṇā pūrvaṃ tapastaptvā kurūdvaha |
havyānāmiva kavyānāṃ sarvasyāpi ca guptaye || 127 ||
items.en: He was made first by Brahma after austerities, O lift of the Kuru line, to guard the offerings to gods and to ancestors, and everything.

items.text:
अश्नन्ति च मुखेनास्य हव्यानि त्रिदिवौकसः ।
कव्यानि चैव पितरः किम्भूतमधिकं ततः ॥ १२८ ॥
items.tr:
aśnanti ca mukhenāsya havyāni tridivaukasaḥ |
kavyāni caiva pitaraḥ kimbhūtamadhikaṃ tataḥ || 128 ||
items.en: The dwellers in heaven eat the offerings through his mouth, and the ancestors their offerings. What is higher than that?

items.text:
भूतानां प्राणिनः श्रेष्ठाः प्राणिनां बुद्धिजीविनः ।
बुद्धिमत्सु नराः श्रेष्ठा नरेषु ब्राह्मणाः स्मृताः ॥ १२९ ॥
items.tr:
bhūtānāṃ prāṇinaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ prāṇināṃ buddhijīvinaḥ |
buddhimatsu narāḥ śreṣṭhā nareṣu brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ || 129 ||
items.en: Of beings, the living are the best; of the living, those who live by understanding; of those with understanding, men; and among men, Brahmins are remembered as best.

items.text:
ब्राह्मणेषु च विद्वांसो विद्वत्सु कृतबुद्धयः ।
कृतबुद्धिषु कर्तारः कर्तृषु ब्रह्मवेदिनः ॥ १३० ॥
items.tr:
brāhmaṇeṣu ca vidvāṃso vidvatsu kṛtabuddhayaḥ |
kṛtabuddhiṣu kartāraḥ kartṛṣu brahmavedinaḥ || 130 ||
items.en: Among Brahmins the learned; among the learned, those of settled mind; among these, those who act; among those who act, the knowers of Brahman.

items.text:
जन्म विप्रस्य राजेन्द्र धमार्थमिह कथ्यते ।
उत्पन्नः सर्वसिद्धयर्थं याति ब्रह्मसदो नृप ॥ १३१ ॥
items.tr:
janma viprasya rājendra dhamārthamiha kathyate |
utpannaḥ sarvasiddhayarthaṃ yāti brahmasado nṛpa || 131 ||
items.en: The birth of a Brahmin, O best of kings, is said to be for the sake of duty here. Born for the success of all, he goes to Brahma's hall, O king.

items.text:
स चापि जायमानस्तु पृथिव्यामिह जायते ।
भूतानां प्रभवायैव धर्मकोशस्य गुप्तये ॥ १३२ ॥
items.tr:
sa cāpi jāyamānastu pṛthivyāmiha jāyate |
bhūtānāṃ prabhavāyaiva dharmakośasya guptaye || 132 ||
items.en: And being born, he is born on earth for the welfare of beings and to guard the treasury of duty.

items.text:
सर्वं हि ब्राह्मणस्येदं यत्किञ्चित्पृथिवीगतम् ।
जन्मना चोत्तमेनेदं सर्वं वै ब्राह्मणोऽर्हति ॥ १३३ ॥
items.tr:
sarvaṃ hi brāhmaṇasyedaṃ yatkiñcitpṛthivīgatam |
janmanā cottamenedaṃ sarvaṃ vai brāhmaṇo'rhati || 133 ||
items.en: All that is on earth belongs to the Brahmin. By his excellent birth, the Brahmin deserves all this.

items.text:
स्वकीयं ब्राह्मणो भुङ्क्ते विदधाति च सुव्रत ।
करुणां कुर्वतस्तस्य भुञ्जन्ती हेतरे जनाः ॥ १३४ ॥
items.tr:
svakīyaṃ brāhmaṇo bhuṅkte vidadhāti ca suvrata |
karuṇāṃ kurvatastasya bhuñjantī hetare janāḥ || 134 ||
items.en: The Brahmin eats his own and gives, O one of good vows. Other people live eating what he, in his kindness, lets them have.

items.text:
त्रयाणामिह वर्णानां भावाभावाय वै द्विजः ।
भवेद्राजन्न सन्देहस्तुष्टो भावाय वै द्विजः ॥ १३५ ॥
items.tr:
trayāṇāmiha varṇānāṃ bhāvābhāvāya vai dvijaḥ |
bhavedrājanna sandehastuṣṭo bhāvāya vai dvijaḥ || 135 ||
items.en: The Brahmin can bring about the rise or fall of the other three classes, O king, without doubt. When pleased, he brings prosperity.

items.text:
अभावाय भवेत्क्रुद्धस्तस्मात्पूज्यतमो हि सः ।
ब्राह्मणे सति नान्यस्य प्रभुत्वं विद्यते नृप । . ॥ १३६ ॥
items.tr:
abhāvāya bhavetkruddhastasmātpūjyatamo hi saḥ |
brāhmaṇe sati nānyasya prabhutvaṃ vidyate nṛpa | . || 136 ||
items.en: When angry, he brings ruin; therefore he is most worthy of honour. When a Brahmin is present, no one else has lordship, O king.

items.text:
कामात्करोत्यसौ कर्म कामगश्च नृपोत्तम ।
तस्माद्वृन्दारकपुरी तस्मादपि महः पुनः ॥ १३७ ॥
items.tr:
kāmātkarotyasau karma kāmagaśca nṛpottama |
tasmādvṛndārakapurī tasmādapi mahaḥ punaḥ || 137 ||
items.en: He acts from desire and goes where he wishes, O best of kings. From that [he reaches] the city of the gods, and then greater glory.

items.text:
महर्लोकाज्जनोलोकं ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ।
ब्रह्मत्वं च महाबाहो याति विप्रो न संशयः ॥ १३८ ॥
items.tr:
maharlokājjanolokaṃ brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati |
brahmatvaṃ ca mahābāho yāti vipro na saṃśayaḥ || 138 ||
items.en: From the world of glory he goes to the world of Janas and to Brahma's world. The Brahmin attains the state of Brahman, O mighty-armed one, without doubt.

items.speaker: शतानीक उवाच
items.text: ब्रह्मत्वं नाम दुष्प्रापं ब्रह्मलोकेषु सुव्रत ॥ १३९ ॥
items.tr: brahmatvaṃ nāma duṣprāpaṃ brahmalokeṣu suvrata || 139 ||
items.en: The state of Brahman is hard to reach, O one of good vows, in the worlds of Brahma.

items.text:
ब्रह्मत्वं कीदृशं विप्रो ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ।
नाममात्रोऽथ किं विप्रो ब्रह्मत्वं ब्रह्मणः सदा ॥
याति ब्रह्मन्गुणाः के स्युर्ब्रह्मप्राप्तौ ममोच्यताम् ॥ १४० ॥
items.tr:
brahmatvaṃ kīdṛśaṃ vipro brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati |
nāmamātro'tha kiṃ vipro brahmatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sadā ||
yāti brahmanguṇāḥ ke syurbrahmaprāptau mamocyatām || 140 ||
items.en: What is the state of Brahman like? How does a Brahmin go to Brahma's world? Is a Brahmin only a name? What are the qualities by which he reaches the state of Brahman? Tell me, O Brahmin, how it is gained.

items.text: साधुसाधु महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ॥ १४१ ॥
items.tr: sādhusādhu mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ || 141 ||
items.speaker: सुमन्तुरुवाच
items.en: Well said, well said, O mighty-armed one. Hear my excellent answer.

items.text:
ये प्रोक्ता वेदशास्त्रेषु संस्कारा ब्राह्मणस्य तु ।
गर्भाधानादयो ये च संस्कारा यस्य पार्थिव ॥ १४२ ॥
items.tr:
ye proktā vedaśāstreṣu saṃskārā brāhmaṇasya tu |
garbhādhānādayo ye ca saṃskārā yasya pārthiva || 142 ||
items.en: The rites of refinement told in the Vedas and law books for a Brahmin, beginning with conception, those that belong to him, O king,

items.text:
चत्वारिंशतथाष्टौ च निर्वृत्ताः शास्त्रतो नृप ।
स याति ब्रह्मणः स्थानं ब्राह्मणत्वं च मानद॥
संस्काराः सर्वथा हेतुर्ब्रह्मत्वे नात्र संशयः ॥ १४३ ॥
items.tr:
catvāriṃśatathāṣṭau ca nirvṛttāḥ śāstrato nṛpa |
sa yāti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ brāhmaṇatvaṃ ca mānada||
saṃskārāḥ sarvathā heturbrahmatve nātra saṃśayaḥ || 143 ||
items.en: forty and eight, completed according to scripture, O king: he reaches the place of Brahma and the state of a Brahmin, O giver of honour. These rites are in every way the cause of the state of Brahman, without doubt.

items.speaker: शतानीक उवाच
items.text:
संस्काराः के मता ब्रह्मन्ब्रह्मत्वे ब्राह्मणस्य तु ।
शंस मे द्विजशार्दूलं कौतुकं हि महन्मम ॥ १४४ ॥
items.tr:
saṃskārāḥ ke matā brahmanbrahmatve brāhmaṇasya tu |
śaṃsa me dvijaśārdūlaṃ kautukaṃ hi mahanmama || 144 ||
items.en: Which rites are held to lead a Brahmin to the state of Brahman, O Brahmin? Tell me, O tiger of the twice-born, for my curiosity is great.

items.text:
साधुसाधु महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
ये प्रोक्ता वेदशास्त्रेषु संस्कारा ब्राह्मणस्य तु ॥
मनीषिभिर्महाबाहो शृणु सर्वानशेषतः ॥ १४५ ॥
items.tr:
sādhusādhu mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
ye proktā vedaśāstreṣu saṃskārā brāhmaṇasya tu ||
manīṣibhirmahābāho śṛṇu sarvānaśeṣataḥ || 145 ||
items.speaker: सुमन्तुरुवाच
items.en: Well said, well said, O mighty-armed one. Hear my excellent answer. The rites told in the Vedas and law books for a Brahmin, declared by the wise, O mighty-armed one, hear all of them in full.

items.text:
गर्भाधानं पुंसवनं सीमन्तोन्नयनं तथा ।
जातकर्मान्नाशनं च चूडोपनयनं नृप ॥ १४६ ॥
items.tr:
garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaṃ tathā |
jātakarmānnāśanaṃ ca cūḍopanayanaṃ nṛpa || 146 ||
items.en: Conception, the rite for a male child, the parting of the hair, birth rite, first feeding, tonsure and initiation, O king,

items.text:
ब्रह्मव्रतानि चत्वारि स्नानं च तदनन्तरम् ।
सधर्मचारिणीयोगो यज्ञानां कर्म मानद ॥ १४७ ॥
items.tr:
brahmavratāni catvāri snānaṃ ca tadanantaram |
sadharmacāriṇīyogo yajñānāṃ karma mānada || 147 ||
items.en: the four Vedic vows, then the bath [ending study], marriage with a wife of the same duty, and the sacrifices, O giver of honour,

items.text:
पञ्चानां कार्यमित्याहुरात्मनः श्रेयसे नृप ।
देवपितृमनुष्याणां भूतानां ब्राह्मणस्तथा ॥ १४८ ॥
items.tr:
pañcānāṃ kāryamityāhurātmanaḥ śreyase nṛpa |
devapitṛmanuṣyāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ brāhmaṇastathā || 148 ||
items.en: are said to be the duty of five, for one's own good, O king: of gods, ancestors, men, [other] beings, and the Brahmin.

items.text:
एतेषां चाष्टकाकर्म पार्वणश्राद्धमेव हि ।
श्रावणी चाग्रहायणी चैत्री चाश्वयुजी तथा ॥ १४९ ॥
items.tr:
eteṣāṃ cāṣṭakākarma pārvaṇaśrāddhameva hi |
śrāvaṇī cāgrahāyaṇī caitrī cāśvayujī tathā || 149 ||
items.en: Of these are also the Ashtaka rite and the Parvana ancestor offering, and the Shravani, Agrahayani, Chaitri and Ashvayuji rites.

items.text:
पाकयज्ञास्तथा सप्त अग्न्याधानं च सत्क्रिया ।
अग्निहोत्रं तथा राजन्दर्शं च विधुसञ्क्षये ॥ १५० ॥
items.tr:
pākayajñāstathā sapta agnyādhānaṃ ca satkriyā |
agnihotraṃ tathā rājandarśaṃ ca vidhusañkṣaye || 150 ||
items.en: Also the seven cooked-food sacrifices, the setting up of the fires and the good rites, the daily fire offering, O king, and the new-moon sacrifice at the moon's disappearance,

items.text:
पौर्णमासं च राजेन्द्र चातुर्मास्यानि चापि हि ।
निरूपणं पशुवधं तथा सौत्रामणीति च ॥ १५१ ॥
items.tr:
paurṇamāsaṃ ca rājendra cāturmāsyāni cāpi hi |
nirūpaṇaṃ paśuvadhaṃ tathā sautrāmaṇīti ca || 151 ||
items.en: the full-moon sacrifice, O best of kings, the four-monthly sacrifices, the animal sacrifice and Sautramani.

items.text:
हविर्यज्ञास्तथा सप्त तेषां चापि हि सत्क्रिया ।
अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोमस्तथोक्थ्यः षोडशीं विदुः ॥ १५२ ॥
items.tr:
haviryajñāstathā sapta teṣāṃ cāpi hi satkriyā |
agniṣṭomo'tyagniṣṭomastathokthyaḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ viduḥ || 152 ||
items.en: The seven offering sacrifices, and their good rites: Agnishtoma, Atyagnishtoma, Ukthya and Shodashi are known,

items.text:
वाजपेयोऽतिरात्रश्च आप्तोर्यामेति वै स्मृतः।
संस्कारेषु स्थिताः सप्त सोमाः कुरुकुलोद्वह ॥ १५३ ॥
items.tr:
vājapeyo'tirātraśca āptoryāmeti vai smṛtaḥ|
saṃskāreṣu sthitāḥ sapta somāḥ kurukulodvaha || 153 ||
items.en: Vajapeya, Atiratra and Aptoryama, as remembered. The seven Soma sacrifices stand among the rites, O lift of the Kuru line.

items.text:
इत्येते द्विजसंस्काराश्चत्वारिंशन्नृपोत्तम ।
अष्टौ चात्मगुणास्तात शृणु तानपि भारत ॥ १५४ ॥
items.tr:
ityete dvijasaṃskārāścatvāriṃśannṛpottama |
aṣṭau cātmaguṇāstāta śṛṇu tānapi bhārata || 154 ||
items.en: These are the forty rites of the twice-born, O best of kings. And there are eight qualities of the self, my dear; hear them too, O descendant of Bharata.

items.text:
अनसूया दया क्षान्तिरनायासं च मङ्गलम् ।
अकार्पण्यं तथा शौचमस्पृहा च कुरूद्वह ॥ १५५ ॥
items.tr:
anasūyā dayā kṣāntiranāyāsaṃ ca maṅgalam |
akārpaṇyaṃ tathā śaucamaspṛhā ca kurūdvaha || 155 ||
items.en: Freedom from envy, compassion, patience, freedom from strain, auspiciousness, generosity, purity and freedom from greed, O lift of the Kurus.

items.text:
य एतेऽष्टगुणास्तात कीर्त्यन्ते वै मनीषिभिः ।
एतेषां लक्षणं वीर शृणु सर्वमशेषतः ॥ १५६ ॥
items.tr:
ya ete'ṣṭaguṇāstāta kīrtyante vai manīṣibhiḥ |
eteṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vīra śṛṇu sarvamaśeṣataḥ || 156 ||
items.en: These eight qualities, my dear, are named by the wise. Hear fully the mark of each, O hero.

items.text:
न गुणान्गुणिनो हन्ति न स्तौत्यात्मगुणानपि ।
प्रहष्यन्ते नान्यदोषैरनसूया प्रकीर्तिता ॥ १५७ ॥
items.tr:
na guṇānguṇino hanti na stautyātmaguṇānapi |
prahaṣyante nānyadoṣairanasūyā prakīrtitā || 157 ||
items.en: One who neither harms the good qualities of the virtuous, nor praises his own qualities, nor rejoices at others' faults, is said to be free from envy.

items.text:
अपरे बन्धुवर्गे वा मित्रे द्वेष्टरि वा सदा ।
आत्मवद्वर्तनं यत्स्यात्सा दया परिकीर्तिता ॥ १५८ ॥
items.tr:
apare bandhuvarge vā mitre dveṣṭari vā sadā |
ātmavadvartanaṃ yatsyātsā dayā parikīrtitā || 158 ||
items.en: Behaviour toward strangers, relatives, friends or enemies as toward oneself, is called compassion.

items.text:
वाचा मनसि काये च दुःखेनोत्पादितेन च ।
न कुप्यति न चाप्रीतिः सा क्षमा परिकीर्तिता ॥ १५९ ॥
items.tr:
vācā manasi kāye ca duḥkhenotpāditena ca |
na kupyati na cāprītiḥ sā kṣamā parikīrtitā || 159 ||
items.en: Not becoming angry or resentful when pain is caused by word, mind or body, is called patience.

items.text:
अभक्ष्यपरिहारश्च संसर्गश्चाप्यनिन्दितैः ।
आचारे च व्यवस्थानं शौचमेतत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ १६० ॥
items.tr:
abhakṣyaparihāraśca saṃsargaścāpyaninditaiḥ |
ācāre ca vyavasthānaṃ śaucametatprakīrtitam || 160 ||
items.en: Avoiding forbidden food, keeping company with the blameless, and standing firm in right conduct: this is called purity.

items.text:
शरीरं पीड्यते येन शुभेनापि च कर्मणा ।
अत्यन्तं तन्न कुर्वीत अनायासः स उच्यते ॥ १६१ ॥
items.tr:
śarīraṃ pīḍyate yena śubhenāpi ca karmaṇā |
atyantaṃ tanna kurvīta anāyāsaḥ sa ucyate || 161 ||
items.en: One should not do, to excess, any act, even a good one, that torments the body. That is called freedom from strain.

items.text:
प्रशस्ताचरणं नित्यमप्रशस्तविवर्जनम् ।
एतद्धि मङ्गलं प्रोक्तं मुनिभिर्ब्रह्मवादिभिः ॥ १६२ ॥
items.tr:
praśastācaraṇaṃ nityamapraśastavivarjanam |
etaddhi maṅgalaṃ proktaṃ munibhirbrahmavādibhiḥ || 162 ||
items.en: Always doing praiseworthy things and avoiding the blameworthy: this is what sages who speak of Brahman call auspiciousness.

items.text:
स्तोकादपि प्रदातव्यमदीनेनान्तरात्मना ।
अहन्यहनि यत्किंचिदकार्पण्यं तदुच्यते ॥ १६३ ॥
items.tr:
stokādapi pradātavyamadīnenāntarātmanā |
ahanyahani yatkiṃcidakārpaṇyaṃ taducyate || 163 ||
items.en: Giving even a little each day, with an unbroken mind, is called generosity.

items.text:
यथोत्पन्नेन सन्तुष्टः स्वल्पेनाप्यथ वस्तुना ।
अहिंसया परस्वेषु साऽस्पृहा परिकीर्तिता ॥ १६४ ॥
items.tr:
yathotpannena santuṣṭaḥ svalpenāpyatha vastunā |
ahiṃsayā parasveṣu sā'spṛhā parikīrtitā || 164 ||
items.en: Being content with whatever one has, even if small, and not harming others' property: this is called freedom from greed.

items.text:
वपुर्यस्य तु इत्येतैः संस्कारैः संस्कृतं द्विजः ।
ब्रह्मत्वमिह सम्प्राप्य ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ॥ १६५ ॥
items.tr:
vapuryasya tu ityetaiḥ saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ dvijaḥ |
brahmatvamiha samprāpya brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati || 165 ||
items.en: A twice-born whose body is refined by these rites, having gained the state of Brahman here, goes to Brahma's world.

items.text:
वैदिकैः कर्मभिः पुण्यैर्निषेकाद्यैर्द्विजन्मनाम् ।
कार्यः शरीरसंस्कारः पावनः प्रेत्य चेह च ॥ १६६ ॥
items.tr:
vaidikaiḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyairniṣekādyairdvijanmanām |
kāryaḥ śarīrasaṃskāraḥ pāvanaḥ pretya ceha ca || 166 ||
items.en: By holy Vedic rites, beginning with conception, for the twice-born, the rites of refining the body should be done; they purify here and after death.

items.text:
गर्भशुद्धिं ततः प्राप्य धर्मं चाश्रमलक्षणम् ।
याति मुक्तिं न सन्देहः पुराणेऽस्मिन्नृपोत्तम ॥ १६७ ॥
items.tr:
garbhaśuddhiṃ tataḥ prāpya dharmaṃ cāśramalakṣaṇam |
yāti muktiṃ na sandehaḥ purāṇe'sminnṛpottama || 167 ||
items.en: Having then gained purity of birth, and the duty marked by the stages of life, one reaches liberation without doubt, according to this Purana, O best of kings.

items.text:
उशन्ति कुरुशार्दूल ब्राह्मणा नात्र संशयः ।
आश्रितानां विशेषेण ये नित्यं स्वस्तिवादिनः ॥ १६८ ॥
items.tr:
uśanti kuruśārdūla brāhmaṇā nātra saṃśayaḥ |
āśritānāṃ viśeṣeṇa ye nityaṃ svastivādinaḥ || 168 ||
items.en: Brahmins, O tiger of the Kurus, are without doubt desired, especially by those who depend on them and are always speaking blessings.

items.text:
निकटस्थान्द्विजान्हित्वा योऽन्यान्पूजयति द्विजान् ।
सिद्धं पापं तदपमानात्तद्वक्तुं नैव शक्यते ॥ १६९ ॥
items.tr:
nikaṭasthāndvijānhitvā yo'nyānpūjayati dvijān |
siddhaṃ pāpaṃ tadapamānāttadvaktuṃ naiva śakyate || 169 ||
items.en: One who, leaving aside the twice-born near him, honours other twice-born, incurs sin through that insult; it cannot be told.

items.text:
तस्मात्सदा समीपस्थः सम्पूज्यो विधिवन्नृप ।
पूजयेदतिथींस्तद्वदन्नपानादिदानतः ॥ १७० ॥
items.tr:
tasmātsadā samīpasthaḥ sampūjyo vidhivannṛpa |
pūjayedatithīṃstadvadannapānādidānataḥ || 170 ||
items.en: Therefore one who is near should always be honoured by rule, O king. In the same way one should honour guests with gifts of food, drink and the like.

items.text:
ब्राह्मणः सर्ववर्णानां ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठस्तथोत्तमः ।
एवमस्मिन्पुराणे तु संस्कारान्ब्राह्मणस्य तु ॥ १७१ ॥
items.tr:
brāhmaṇaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhastathottamaḥ |
evamasminpurāṇe tu saṃskārānbrāhmaṇasya tu || 171 ||
items.en: The Brahmin is the eldest, best and highest of all classes. In this way, in this Purana, the rites of a Brahmin [are told].

items.text:
शृणोति यश्च जानाति यश्चापि पठते सदा ।
ऋद्धिं वृद्धिं तथा कीर्तिं प्राप्येह श्रियमुत्तमाम् ॥ १७२ ॥
items.tr:
śṛṇoti yaśca jānāti yaścāpi paṭhate sadā |
ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathā kīrtiṃ prāpyeha śriyamuttamām || 172 ||
items.en: One who hears, knows or always recites this gains here prosperity, growth, fame and supreme fortune.

items.text:
धनं धान्यं यशश्चापि पुत्रान्बन्धून्सुरूपताम् ।
सावित्रं लोकमासाद्य ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥ १७३ ॥
items.tr:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ yaśaścāpi putrānbandhūnsurūpatām |
sāvitraṃ lokamāsādya brahmalokamavāpnuyāt || 173 ||
items.en: Wealth, grain, glory, sons, relatives and good looks; having reached the world of the sun, one will attain Brahma's world.

en_summary: Sumantu tells Shatanika that this Purana has five parts and five marks, including creation, secondary creation and lineages, and he lists the fourteen and eighteen branches of learning. He then describes creation: the dark unmanifest world, the golden egg, Brahma, the elements, the first sages, the beings of all kinds and the four classes with their duties. He explains the divisions of time, from a blink of the eye to a day of Brahma, and the four ages with their changing duties and lifespans. The chapter ends with the forty rites of a Brahmin, the eight inner qualities, and the rewards of hearing it.
